Subtask Summary: For optical and electrical characterizations, free-standing TCCs (FS- TCC) samples were prepared by laminating the composite mixture between glass substrates covered with polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) release liners. Contaminants and residue on the glass substrates were removed by manually scrubbing the surface with a Kimwipe saturated with isopropanol, followed by acetone and methanol, and dried using N . The release liners were tarped over glass substrates (5 cm ´ 5 cm) and adhered on 2 the rear of the substrate along the four edges such that the film was under tension and flush across the front surface. Using these substrates, FS-TCC samples were prepared according to the aforementioned procedure (subtask 1.1) using 45-53µm Ag-PMMA microsphere fillers. The resulting samples were cut into 2.54 cm ´ 2.54 cm (approx. 6.45 cm2) coupons for optical and electrical characterizations. Optoelectronic Properties of TCCs – Considering the electrically insulating nature of the transparent epoxy used in this study, the conductivity of TCCs relies exclusively on the dispersed conductive media. Recently, Ag-PMMA microsphere fillers gained interest in the PV community due to their outstanding and reproducible optoelectronic performance.147,148 These early demonstrations implemented Ag-PMMA as an electronic interconnect to form multijunction PV devices.58–63 To account for the inherent distribution of microsphere diameters (90% in the 45-53µm range), optimized assembly processes typically comprised high-temperature lamination to melt and compress the entire microsphere population between the sub-cells.
